title: Reducing the Urge to be Physically Active in Patients with Anorexia Nervosa through Virtual Reality: A Randomized-Controlled Feasibility Trial
summary: The study investigates the feasibility of a novel virtual reality (VR)-based intervention to alleviate the urge to to be physically active during the treatment of anorexia nervosa (AN). Patients with AN often report an intense urge to be active. However, exercising and other intense movements conflict with the treatment goal of restroring a healthy body weight. The urge to be active should therefore be alleviated by other means. The main objective of this study is to assess the feasibility of a randomized controlled trial (RCT) that will investigate the efficacy of the VR intervention as an add-on treatment.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The trial will include patients admitted to inpatient treatment with a diagnosis of restricting or binge-eating/purging type AN according to ICD-10 criteria (i.e., F50.00 and F50.01), with a body mass index (BMI) ≤ 17.5 kg/m², aged 18 years or older, able and willing to provide informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
We will exclude patients with AN who present with severe comorbid psychiatric or
somatic disorders or other conditions that may interfere with study protocol adherence and/or ability to provide informed consent (e.g., severe depression, acute suicidal tendencies, relevant difficulties in spoken and written German).
